title: Localizing the scalar map to a finite tensor factor
statement: Let A and D be commutative rings in universe u and B a commutative A-algebra in any universe. Assume B is finite as an A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and D is an A-algebra. Let J be an ideal of D, e any element of T=D tensor_A B, and assume that for every t in T there is d in D with t-d in (1-e)+JT. There exist a commutative ring C in universe u and a flat ring map psi:D -> C such that D/J -> C/JC is bijective, and C -> (C tensor_A B)/(1-m(e)) is surjective, where C has its composite A-algebra structure and m is the tensor map psi tensor identity. No idempotency or Jacobson hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EM0, proof of lemma-helper-finite, Nakayama localization making the first factor scalar map surjective; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EM0

proof.text: Set T=D tensor_A B, Q=T/(1-e), and let N be the D-linear range of the structure map D -> Q. Mathlib finite base change and quotient instances make Q a finite D-module. The hypothesis and the quotient membership criterion give top <= N + J*top.

Apply Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_smul_le_of_fg_of_le_sup with the finitely generated submodule N′ and P both equal to top. Obtain g with g-1 in J and g*Q contained in N. Thus for each t in T there is d in D whose scalar image equals g times the class of t.

Construct C=D[1/g]. Its structure map is flat. Since g=1 modulo J, IsLocalization.Away.lift defines C -> D/J, factoring through C/JC. The resulting inverse to D/J -> C/JC is checked on representatives and by localization ringHom_ext.

The tensor map m induces Q -> (C tensor_A B)/(1-m(e)). For a pure generator 1 tensor b, the Nakayama relation says its product with the scalar g is a scalar d. Multiply by the scalar inverse of g to express this generator as a scalar. Every c tensor b is c times such a generator, and tensor induction handles zero and sums. Thus the new structure map is surjective.

theorem exists_flat_tensor_factor_localization
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {D : Type u}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A D]
    [Module.Finite A B] (J : Ideal D) (e : TensorProduct A D B)
    (h : ∀ t : TensorProduct A D B, ∃ d : D,
      t - algebraMap D (TensorProduct A D B) d ∈
        Ideal.span {1 - e} ⊔ J.map (algebraMap D (TensorProduct A D B))) :
    ∃ (C : CommRingCat.{u}) (ψ : D →+* C),
      letI : Algebra A C := (ψ.comp (algebraMap A D)).toAlgebra
      let ψA : D →ₐ[A] C := { ψ with commutes' := fun _ => rfl }
      let m := Algebra.TensorProduct.map ψA (AlgHom.id A B)
      ψ.Flat ∧
        Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (J.map ψ) ψ Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
        Function.Surjective
          (algebraMap C (TensorProduct A C B ⧸ Ideal.span {1 - m e}))
